parsed.headline: Toronto City Clerk certifies 2026 municipal election results

pages.text: Toronto City Clerk John D. Elvidge has certified the official results for Toronto’s 2026 municipal election. The official declaration of results, which indicates the total number of votes received by each candidate, is available on the Toronto Elections Results webpage. Poll-by-poll results, detailing votes cast during advance voting, by mail, and at each election day voting place, are also available through the city's website. Final voter statistics, including the official number of eligible voters following all revisions to the voters’ list, are scheduled to be available within 30 days of the election. The 2026-2030 term of Toronto City Council is set to begin on October 25, 2026. New members of Council will make their Declaration of Office privately with the City Clerk prior to the first meeting of City Council, which is scheduled for October 28, 2026.

parsed.headline: Africa CDC urges coordinated action as Ebola outbreak exceeds 10,000 cases

pages.text: The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) has called for strengthened cross-border cooperation and coordinated responses as an Ebola outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo virus spreads beyond the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). The call was made during an extraordinary virtual meeting of African health ministers on October 28, 2026, to discuss measures for improved surveillance, preparedness, and containment efforts. Africa CDC Director-General Dr. Jean Kaseya stated the outbreak is an economic destabilizer affecting trade, supply chains, and household livelihoods. According to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the outbreak had recorded 10,172 confirmed cases and 4,932 confirmed deaths across five affected countries and territories as of October 26. The CDC described the event as the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record, following the 2014–2016 West African epidemic. The DRC has accounted for the overwhelming majority of cases and deaths since the outbreak began in May 2026. Congolese health authorities reported on October 27, 2026, that the country had recorded 10,060 infections and 4,887 deaths, noting the epidemic's fatality rate appears close to 50 percent according to the Congolese National Institute of Public Health. The outbreak was first detected in the northeastern province of Ituri and has since spread across the north and east of the country. Challenges to containment include the lack of approved vaccines or specific treatments for the Bundibugyo variant. The outbreak has also been reported in Kenya, Nigeria, and Uganda, with cases also associated with the wider outbreak in France. In Kenya, nine infections and two deaths have been confirmed. Nigeria confirmed its first case on October 20, involving a 42-year-old Swiss woman who entered from Uganda; she was evacuated to a hospital in Geneva on October 26, 2026. Uganda has recorded 20 confirmed cases traced to a patient from the DRC. During the October 28 meeting, Simbisile Kulu, South Africa’s Director-General for Health, described the spread as a continental health security concern and noted that South Africa is strengthening surveillance, laboratory capacity, and border preparedness.

parsed.headline: President Mahama commends Putin’s willingness to resume trilateral Ukraine talks

pages.text: Addressing the Third Russia–Africa Summit in Moscow, Ghanaian President John Dramani Mahama commended Russian President Vladimir Putin for his willingness to resume trilateral talks regarding the conflict with Ukraine. Mahama expressed appreciation for Putin's call for a lasting peace agreement and security for both Russia and Ukraine, while calling for the amicable resolution of global conflicts to prevent death, suffering, and the disruption of global logistics and value chains. During the summit, which was chaired by Putin, Mahama also called for international cooperation against terrorism, specifically within the Alliance of Sahelian States. Reaffirming Ghana’s policy of non-alignment, Mahama stated that the country seeks partnerships that advance its development priorities.

parsed.headline: Climate financing in Bangladesh falls short of estimated needs

pages.text: Bangladesh's National Adaptation Plan (NAP) estimates that nearly US$230 billion (approximately Tk 28.52 trillion) will be required by 2050 to address climate challenges. However, the climate-related allocation for 25 ministries and divisions for the 2026–27 fiscal year is set at Tk 517.46 billion. Of that amount, the government-financed Climate Change Trust Fund has received Tk 1 billion. Additionally, a large portion of international public climate finance is provided in the form of loans.

In Sirajganj town, a solar-powered water pump installed two years ago through a local NGO initiative funded by a climate fund serves a slum in Amlapara. Residents, including Maksuda Begum and Rahela Khatun, reported that the pump has reduced difficulties in accessing water compared to the previous municipal supply line. While the project has impacted the Amlapara slum, local residents and municipal officials state that there are approximately 30 slums in the town and no other slum currently has a similar facility.

parsed.headline: Jordan and Syria disagree over October 26 attacks in southern Syria that killed civilians

pages.text: Jordan and Syria have offered conflicting accounts regarding Jordanian air strikes on the southern Syrian regions of Deraa and Suwayda on the evening of October 26, 2026. Jordan stated its air force killed more than 20 ISIL (ISIS) fighters in retaliatory strikes against what it described as “dens of terrorist organisations in southern Syria.” According to Jordanian authorities, these strikes were linked to suspects accused of an attack on a Greek Orthodox church in the Karak governorate, approximately 120km (75 miles) southwest of Amman, which killed nine people and wounded at least 34 others. Jordanian King Abdullah II promised to respond to the church attack with an “iron fist.” However, following the strikes, images circulated in Syria of a slain grandmother and her three grandchildren, contributing to public anger. Navvar Saban, a researcher in security and military affairs at the Arab Center for Contemporary Syrian Studies, told Al Jazeera that the anger reflects an expectation that authorities in Damascus should protect Syrians and demand answers when they are harmed. Saban noted that if the public perceives Damascus as prioritizing its relationship with Jordan over accountability, the anger could turn inward.

parsed.headline: Electric hydrofoil boats are being deployed in the United States

pages.text: In New York Harbor, Vessev is operating fully electric hydrofoil boats. Eric Laakmann, the chief executive and co-founder of Vessev, described the vessels as a curiosity at the moment. These boats utilize underwater wings to lift their hulls approximately a foot and a half above the water surface as they accelerate, a process Laakmann referred to as a takeoff. This design is intended to dramatically reduce drag, which is a significant obstacle to energy efficiency in maritime travel. Replacing diesel-powered ferries with electric vessels could reduce emissions and improve air quality. However, electrifying boats presents challenges because batteries are heavy, and that additional weight increases the power required to move a vessel.

parsed.headline: Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight carrying Prime Minister Tarique Rahman departs Narita for Dhaka after five-hour delay

pages.text: A Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight carrying Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and his entourage departed from Narita International Airport in Japan for Dhaka on Thursday, approximately five hours behind schedule, following a technical fault. The aircraft, flight BG 377, took off at around 10:45 pm local time in Japan, according to a member of the prime minister’s entourage who confirmed the information to Prothom Alo. Biman’s public relations department stated in a press release that the flight had safely taken off after the technical fault was repaired by Biman engineers and Japanese technicians. The airline had previously issued a press release around 5:00 pm stating the flight was delayed due to the fault while flight operations and engineering teams worked to resolve the issue. The flight was originally scheduled to depart at approximately 6:00 pm local time on Thursday following a four-day state visit to Tokyo. The aircraft was reported ready for departure at around 10:15 pm local time after repairs were completed. According to the airline, the flight took off at 7:55 pm Bangladesh time and is scheduled to land in Dhaka at 3:00 am on 30 October.

parsed.headline: Experts warn US climate forecasting capacity hampered by NOAA cuts amid El Niño risks

pages.text: Former government officials and scientists have warned that sweeping cuts to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) have severely hampered the United States' capacity to forecast, research, and respond to extreme weather events. These warnings come as the country faces potential hazards fueled by a potentially historic El Niño this winter. Since January 2025, the agency has lost approximately 20% of its staff. Under President Donald Trump, the agency has seen slashed staff levels, canceled contracts and grants, and the shutdown of research laboratories and databases. Tom Di Liberto, a former NOAA climate scientist and current media director of Climate Central, stated that the system has not been tested since the cuts occurred and questioned whether the country can handle potential coast-to-coast extremes this winter. The National Weather Service, which is housed within NOAA, has also been affected; weather stations have delayed data collection and cut operating hours, while hundreds of technical and meteorological positions remain vacant across its 122 forecast offices. Within NOAA, reports indicate a volatile environment has led to increased burnout and plummeting morale. This reduction in capacity coincides with a super El Niño, a phenomenon of warmer than average equatorial sea surface temperatures, which is expected to strengthen through the northern hemisphere’s autumn and winter. The phenomenon has the potential to supercharge storms in parts of the American west, raise sea levels in California by up to a foot, and contribute to flash floods, landslides, and debris flows.
